events.imageAlt: stock image of historical manuscript letters

2026-10-20.text: Prabowo Subianto and Gibran Rakabuming Raka were sworn in as president and vice president of Indonesia, becoming the oldest and the youngest person to assume respective offices.
2026-10-20.title: Prabowo Subianto

2026-10-20.text: Protests broke out across Chad after President Mahamat Déby (pictured) declared his intentions to extend his rule by another two years.
2026-10-20.title: 2022 Chadian protests

2026-10-20.text: First Libyan Civil War: Muammar Gaddafi, the deposed Libyan leader, was captured by rebel forces during the Battle of Sirte, and was killed shortly thereafter.
2026-10-20.title: Libyan civil war (2011)

2026-10-20.text: An earthquake struck the Indian state of Uttarakhand, killing at least 768 people and destroying thousands of homes.
2026-10-20.title: 1991 Uttarkashi earthquake

2026-10-20.text: Aeroflot Flight 6502 crashed on approach to Kurumoch Airport in Samara, Russia (then Kuybyshev in the Soviet Union), killing 70 people on board.
2026-10-20.title: Aeroflot Flight 6502

2026-10-20.text: Soviet Aeroflot Flight 6502 crashed after overrunning the runway at Kuibyshev Airport, killing 70 people on board.
2026-10-20.title: Aeroflot Flight 6502

2026-10-20.text: The Spanish trawler Sonia sank in British waters after a five-hour chase by the Irish Naval Service patrol vessel Aisling, during which almost 600 shots were fired.
2026-10-20.title: Sinking of the Spanish trawler Sonia

2026-10-20.text: During a UEFA Cup match between Spartak Moscow and Haarlem, a large number of attendees trying to leave the Central Lenin Stadium resulted in a stampede that caused 66 deaths.
2026-10-20.title: 1982–83 UEFA Cup

2026-10-20.text: Three members of the American rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd died when their chartered plane crashed in Gillsburg, Mississippi.
2026-10-20.title: Lynyrd Skynyrd

2026-10-20.text: Watergate scandal: Attorney General Elliot Richardson and his deputy William Ruckelshaus resigned after refusing to obey President Richard Nixon's order to have Archibald Cox fired.
2026-10-20.title: Watergate scandal

2026-10-20.text: Experimental results from the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center were published showing that protons were composed of smaller particles, the first evidence of quarks.
2026-10-20.title: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory

2026-10-20.text: Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin filmed an unidentified subject, which they claimed was Bigfoot, at Six Rivers National Forest in California.
2026-10-20.title: Patterson–Gimlin film

2026-10-20.text: World War II: Fulfilling a promise he made two years previously, General Douglas MacArthur landed on Leyte to begin the recapture of the Philippines.
2026-10-20.title: World War II

2026-10-20.text: Pope Pius XII (pictured) published his first encyclical, Summi Pontificatus, which critiqued ideologies such as racism, cultural superiority and totalitarianism.
2026-10-20.title: Pope Pius XII

2026-10-20.text: British woman Mabel Freer was refused entry to Australia after failing a dictation test given in Italian, leading to a debate over Australia's immigration policy.
2026-10-20.title: Mabel Freer

2026-10-20.text: Under the terms of the Pragmatic Sanction, Maria Theresa (pictured) ascended the Habsburg throne.
2026-10-20.title: Pragmatic Sanction of 1713

2026-10-23.text: Myanmar civil war: Burmese military forces launched airstrikes that killed at least 80 concertgoers in Kachin State.
2026-10-23.title: Myanmar civil war (2021–present)

2026-10-23.text: Pakistani journalist Arshad Sharif is shot and killed by local police in Kajiado, Kenya.
2026-10-23.title: Arshad Sharif

2026-10-23.text: An escalator accident in Rome left 24 people injured, mostly fans of the CSKA Moscow football team who were in town for a UEFA Champions League match against Roma.
2026-10-23.title: 2018 Rome escalator accident

2026-10-23.text: Hurricane Patricia, the most intense tropical cyclone on record in the Western Hemisphere, peaked with maximum sustained winds of 215 mph (345 km/h) south of Mexico.
2026-10-23.title: Hurricane Patricia

2026-10-23.text: During the Malaysian motorcycle Grand Prix, Marco Simoncelli (pictured) collided with two other riders, resulting in his death due to serious trauma to the head, neck, and chest.
2026-10-23.title: 2011 Malaysian motorcycle Grand Prix

2026-10-23.text: Grand Theft Auto III was released, helping to popularize open-world and mature-content video games.
2026-10-23.title: Grand Theft Auto III

2026-10-23.text: The runway show for Alexander McQueen's collection The Hunger was staged at London's Natural History Museum.
2026-10-23.title: Alexander McQueen

2026-10-23.text: Vietnam War: Operation Linebacker, a U.S. bombing campaign against North Vietnam in response to its Easter Offensive, ended after five months.
2026-10-23.title: Vietnam War

2026-10-23.text: A screening of Mother India, one of the most influential Indian films in history, was held for President Rajendra Prasad and Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru two days before its release.
2026-10-23.title: Mother India

2026-10-23.text: The Hungarian Revolution began as a peaceful student demonstration that attracted thousands while marching through central Budapest to the parliament building.
2026-10-23.title: Hungarian Revolution of 1956

2026-10-23.text: The State of Vietnam voted in a referendum to become a republic.
2026-10-23.title: State of Vietnam

2026-10-23.text: World War II: Japanese troops began an unsuccessful attempt to recapture Henderson Field on Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands from American forces.
2026-10-23.title: World War II

2026-10-23.text: Jeannette Piccard (pictured) piloted a hot-air balloon flight that reached 57,579 feet (17,550 m), becoming the first woman to fly in the stratosphere.
2026-10-23.title: Jeannette Piccard

2026-10-23.text: Alberto Santos-Dumont flew his biplane 14-bis for 50 metres (160 ft) at an altitude of about four metres (13 ft).
2026-10-23.title: Alberto Santos-Dumont

2026-10-23.text: The inaugural National Women's Rights Convention, presided over by American activist Paulina Wright Davis (pictured), began in Worcester, Massachusetts.
2026-10-23.title: National Women's Rights Convention

2026-10-23.text: War of the Second Coalition: The Ottoman–Albanian forces of Ali Pasha of Janina defeated French troops and captured the town of Preveza at the Battle of Nicopolis.
2026-10-23.title: War of the Second Coalition

2026-10-23.text: Irish Catholic gentry in Ulster tried to seize control of Dublin Castle, the seat of English rule in Ireland, to force concessions to Catholics.
2026-10-23.title: Ulster

2026-10-23.text: The Battle of Grathe Heath ended the Danish Civil War.
2026-10-23.title: Battle of Grathe Heath

2026-10-24.text: Lam Wing-kee, the owner of Causeway Bay Books in Hong Kong, known for publishing political books banned in mainland China, was abducted by Chinese authorities.
2026-10-24.title: Lam Wing-kee

2026-10-24.text: English football club Manchester United defeated rivals Arsenal 2–0 in the Battle of the Buffet, ending the latter's record-breaking unbeaten run.
2026-10-24.title: Manchester United F.C.

2026-10-24.text: The inaugural Afro-Asian Games opened in Hyderabad, with 2,040 athletes from 96 nations competing.
2026-10-24.title: 2003 Afro-Asian Games

2026-10-24.text: In protest against wage discrepancy and unfair employment practices, 90 percent of Iceland's female population went on strike for a day.
2026-10-24.title: Gender pay gap

2026-10-24.text: Three people were killed when falsework collapsed during the construction of the Loddon Bridge in Berkshire, leading to reform of construction practices in the UK.
2026-10-24.title: Falsework

2026-10-24.text: Charges in a military court against generals Dương Văn Đức and Lâm Văn Phát of leading a coup attempt against South Vietnamese leader Nguyễn Khánh, were dropped..
2026-10-24.title: Dương Văn Đức

2026-10-24.text: The cornerstone of the United Nations headquarters was laid in New York City.
2026-10-24.title: Headquarters of the United Nations

2026-10-24.text: The Charter of the United Nations entered into force after being ratified by the five permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of the other signatories.
2026-10-24.title: Charter of the United Nations

2026-10-24.text: World War II: The Japanese battleship Musashi, one of the heaviest and most powerfully armed ever constructed, was sunk by American aircraft during the Battle of Leyte Gulf.
2026-10-24.title: World War II

2026-10-24.text: The George Washington Bridge (pictured), connecting New York City to Fort Lee, New Jersey, and today the world's busiest motor-vehicle bridge, was dedicated.
2026-10-24.title: George Washington Bridge

2026-10-24.text: The Pacification Junta deposed Brazillian president Washington Luís, ending the Brazilian Revolution of 1930.
2026-10-24.title: Brazilian military junta of 1930

2026-10-24.text: On "Black Thursday", the New York Stock Exchange lost 11 percent of its value at the opening bell on very heavy trading, marking the beginning of the Great Depression.
2026-10-24.title: Wall Street crash of 1929

2026-10-24.text: Sir Henry Parkes, Premier of the Colony of New South Wales, gave a speech in which he called for the federation of the six Australian colonies.
2026-10-24.title: Henry Parkes

2026-10-24.text: The Russian ship Dmitry ran aground in Whitby, an incident that inspired the arrival of Count Dracula to England in Bram Stoker's 1897 novel (cover pictured).
2026-10-24.title: Russian ship Dmitry

2026-10-24.text: William Lassell found Umbriel and Ariel, the third and fourth Uranian moons to be discovered.
2026-10-24.title: William Lassell

2026-10-24.text: War of the First Coalition: The Battle of Schliengen was fought between the French and Austrian armies, who both claimed victory.
2026-10-24.title: War of the First Coalition

2026-10-24.text: The Brabant Revolution, sometimes considered to be the first expression of Belgian nationalism, began with the invasion of the Austrian Netherlands by an émigré army from the Dutch Republic.
2026-10-24.title: Brabant Revolution

2026-10-24.text: Qutuz (bust pictured), the sultan of Egypt, was assassinated and replaced by fellow Mamluk leader Baybars.
2026-10-24.title: Qutuz

2026-10-25.text: At 49 days, Liz Truss concluded the shortest tenure as prime minister of the United Kingdom.
2026-10-25.title: Liz Truss

2026-10-25.text: Mount Merapi in Central Java, Indonesia, began an increasingly violent series of eruptions that lasted over a month.
2026-10-25.title: Mount Merapi

2026-10-25.text: Windows XP, one of the most popular and widely used versions of the Microsoft Windows operating system, was released for retail sale.
2026-10-25.title: Windows XP

2026-10-25.text: Heinrich Himmler ordered a crackdown on the Edelweiss Pirates, a nonconformist youth group that assisted army deserters and others hiding from the Nazis.
2026-10-25.title: Heinrich Himmler

2026-10-25.text: USS Tang, the U.S. Navy submarine credited with sinking more ships than any other American submarine, sank when it was struck by its own torpedo.
2026-10-25.title: USS Tang (SS-306)

2026-10-25.text: The Italian cruise liner SS Principessa Mafalda sank when a propeller shaft broke and fractured the hull, resulting in 314 deaths.
2026-10-25.title: SS Principessa Mafalda

2026-10-25.text: The Daily Mail published the Zinoviev letter, a hoax purported to be a directive from Moscow to increase communist agitation.
2026-10-25.title: Daily Mail

2026-10-25.text: Irish playwright and politician Terence MacSwiney died after a hunger strike in Brixton Prison, bringing the Irish struggle for independence to international attention.
2026-10-25.title: Terence MacSwiney

2026-10-25.text: American Civil War: During Price's Missouri Expedition, Union troops defeated Sterling Price's Confederate army in three successive battles: Marais des Cygnes, Mine Creek, and Marmiton River.
2026-10-25.title: American Civil War

2026-10-25.text: Crimean War: The ill-fated Charge of the Light Brigade was decisively repelled by Russian forces during the Battle of Balaclava.
2026-10-25.title: Crimean War

2026-10-25.text: George III became King of Great Britain and Ireland, succeeding his grandfather George II.
2026-10-25.title: George III

2026-10-25.text: Dutch explorer Dirk Hartog left a plate on an island in Shark Bay, the oldest-known artefact of European exploration in Australia still in existence.
2026-10-25.title: Dirk Hartog

2026-10-25.text: Reconquista: Forces under Afonso I of Portugal captured Lisbon from the Moors after a four-month siege in one of the few Christian victories during the Second Crusade.
2026-10-25.title: Reconquista

2026-10-30.text: A magnitude-7.0 earthquake occurred in the Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey, triggering a tsunami and causing 119 deaths.
2026-10-30.title: 2020 Aegean Sea earthquake

2026-10-30.text: American comedians Jon Stewart and Stephen Colbert hosted the Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear in Washington, D.C.
2026-10-30.title: Jon Stewart

2026-10-30.text: After his terminal-cancer diagnosis, Warren Zevon made his last public appearance on the Late Show with David Letterman, giving the advice to "enjoy every sandwich".
2026-10-30.title: Warren Zevon

2026-10-30.text: Michael Jackson released Invincible, his final studio album and the most expensive album ever produced.
2026-10-30.title: Michael Jackson

2026-10-30.text: The Troubles: Three members of the Ulster Defence Association opened fire in a crowded pub during a Halloween party, killing eight people and wounding nineteen others.
2026-10-30.title: The Troubles

2026-10-30.text: The Madrid Conference, an attempt by the international community to revive the Israeli–Palestinian peace process through negotiations, convened.
2026-10-30.title: Madrid Conference of 1991

2026-10-30.text: As the military dictatorship came to an end, Argentina's first democratic election in a decade resulted in Raúl Alfonsín being elected president.
2026-10-30.title: National Reorganization Process

2026-10-30.text: At the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Michael Woodruff performed the first successful kidney transplantation in the United Kingdom.
2026-10-30.title: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh

2026-10-30.text: A luzzu (Maltese fishing boat) overloaded with passengers capsized and sank in the Gozo Channel off Qala, killing 23 of the 27 people on board (monument pictured).
2026-10-30.title: Luzzu

2026-10-30.text: CBS Radio broadcast "The War of the Worlds", a radio drama that newspapers accused of tricking Americans into believing there was an actual Martian invasion.
2026-10-30.title: CBS Radio

2026-10-30.text: Lobengula, King of Matabeleland, granted the Rudd Concession (pictured) to agents of Cecil Rhodes, leading to the creation of the British South Africa Company.
2026-10-30.title: Lobengula

2026-10-30.text: Seventeen-year-old Vilhelm, Prince of Denmark, arrived in Athens to become King George I of Greece (pictured).
2026-10-30.title: Athens

2026-10-30.text: War of the Fourth Coalition: Believing that they were outnumbered, the German garrison at Stettin surrendered to a much smaller French force without a fight.
2026-10-30.title: War of the Fourth Coalition
